modeReason: The top story (a CEO saying the world should accept AI's "bad things" while his own spokesperson deflected a reporter's question about one of them) scores novelty 2 x magnitude 3 x breadth 3 = 18, well above the fresh threshold of 8.
phrase: A top AI company's chief executive said the world should accept 'bad things' from AI. His own spokesperson tried to change the subject when one came up.
phraseAlternatives: A top AI company's boss says some harm is an acceptable price for AI's benefits. When a reporter raised a real one, his spokesperson asked to move on.
The CEO of a top AI company says the world should tolerate AI's 'bad things.' His own team did not want to discuss one specific bad thing.
An AI company's leader argued that hacks and scams are a fair price for progress. His publicist preferred not to discuss an actual one.

brief.concept: A confident company boss tells the world to accept AI's harms as the cost of progress, while his own spokesperson steps in to block a question about one of those harms.
brief.metaphor: The spokesperson's raised speech bubble is a human shield for the company's talking points.

brief.composition: Three generic human cutout figures in a row on kraft card: the executive at a podium on the left beside the tall meter; in the center the spokesperson stands with arms raised, holding a large blank speech bubble that blocks the view toward the reporter on the right, whose small speech bubble with a question mark peeks out from behind it.
brief.alt: An executive speaks at a podium next to a meter with its needle near the top, while a spokesperson in the middle holds up a large blank speech bubble that blocks a reporter's question bubble on the right.
